pathway.title: Churchill Downs Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Business quality is adequate and event-concentrated: Live and Historical Racing earns the largest share of segment profit, and the second quarter produced 37.42% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, so one flagship event and historical racing machine rules in Kentucky and Virginia carry a large part of the debt service capacity. The 16 historical racing venues, ten owned casinos and online wagering give geographic spread that single-asset operators lack. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C04

Cash flow conversion is solid: last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 529.9 million is 45.79% of reported EBITDA, with capital expenditure well below the FY2025 level, but conversion in 2026 benefits from lower project capital and the planned Rockingham and First Turn projects will absorb cash again. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02

Leverage is improving but still material: total debt is 4.08x and net debt 3.94x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, down from 4.83x at 2025-12-31, and cash interest cover is 4.22x against 3.61x. On the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back its share of equity investees' EBITDA, total leverage is 3.79x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01

Liquidity is adequate: unrestricted cash of USD 167 million and about USD 1,111 million of undrawn revolver capacity give 1.83x cover of the USD 700 million notes due in January 2028, but the October 2026 redemption of the 2027 notes was funded from the revolver, so the post-redemption position is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C05

Refinancing depends on the 2028 notes: the revolver and term loan A, USD 1,148 million at 2026-09-30, mature in September 2031 only if notes maturing earlier are refinanced at least 91 days before maturity, a test that falls on 2027-10-16 for the 2028 notes; the longest-dated debt is the USD 500 million term loan B due 2033. No large note maturity falls before January 2028 after the 2027 redemption. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C06

Financial policy is the main judgement: dividends are small, but FY2025 buybacks and dividends took 92.67% of free cash flow with revolver borrowings rising, while payouts were 15.50% in nine months 2026. Sponsor and governance risk is medium, with no sponsor, no documented creditor-adverse action and legal capacity not testable. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C03

cells.text: Three reportable segments: Live and Historical Racing, Wagering Services and Solutions, and Gaming, plus All Other for the captive insurer and corporate costs.
Earnings are spread across racing, wagering technology and casinos, but each depends on state licences and gaming law.
Churchill Downs Racetrack (Kentucky Derby) and 10,190 historical racing machines in 16 venues across Kentucky and Virginia, plus the Chasers poker room in New Hampshire; 47.67% of FY2025 net revenue.
Largest and fastest-growing segment; exposed to Kentucky and Virginia historical racing law, tax and competition.
TwinSpires online horse wagering, United Tote, Exacta central determinant systems and sports betting; 16.69% of FY2025 net revenue.
Technology and wagering income that supports the venues but depends on state licensing and third-party platform agreements.

Ten wholly owned casinos (Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Mississippi, New York, Pennsylvania) plus 61.3% of Midwest Gaming and 50% of Miami Valley Gaming; 35.64% of FY2025 net revenue.
Regional casinos are competitive and regulated; equity income from the two investees is reached only through distributions.
The Kentucky Derby falls in the second quarter, which produced USD 451 million of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA (37.42%); seasonal employees are hired mainly in the second quarter.
Quarter-end balances and single-quarter ratios mislead; use last twelve months.
About 9,000 team members including about 6,600 full-time; about 840 full-time team members are covered by 11 collective bargaining agreements.
No material labour disruption reported; fixed costs persist when revenue falls.

FY2025 capital expenditure of USD 274.9 million, of which USD 204.7 million was project capital; 2026 project capital is expected at USD 160 million to USD 180 million, after USD 180.0 million to USD 220.0 million expected in the annual report.
Growth spending is discretionary but committed projects (Rockingham, First Turn building) compete with debt reduction.
Publicly traded on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under CHDN; about 1,940 shareholders of record at 2026-02-19; no controlling owner or sponsor named in the documents read.
No sponsor support to rely on; capital allocation is set by the board and management.

runs.text: Strength: the business is spread across racing, wagering and casino earnings. Evidence is that Live and Historical Racing, Wagering Services and Solutions and Gaming produced USD 637.0 million, USD 177.3 million and USD 483.0 million of FY2025 segment Adjusted EBITDA, so no single segment exceeds half of the total. The mechanism is that a shock to one segment is cushioned by the others, which supports debt service capacity and refinancing confidence. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 125–126; calculation C04

Strength: cash generation and deleveraging. Evidence is last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 529.9 million and a fall in total debt to reported EBITDA from 4.83x to 4.08x in nine months. The mechanism is that operating cash flow after capital expenditure was applied to the revolver, which shortens the time to a lower leverage level and widens the cushion for the 2028 refinancing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02

Strength: extended bank maturities and ample liquidity at the balance sheet date. Evidence is the September 2026 amendment moving the revolver and term loan A to September 2031 and USD 1,278 million of cash and undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-09-30. The mechanism is that no bank maturity falls before 2031 unless the springing test is triggered, so near-term refinancing pressure is limited. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C05

Weakness: earnings concentration in the Kentucky Derby quarter and in historical racing rules. Evidence is 37.42% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA in the second quarter and a USD 10 million decrease in Central Virginia Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 from competition and a new tax. The mechanism is that a weather, regulatory or tax event concentrates loss in a few states and one quarter, so leverage and liquidity can move sharply. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; EX-99.1_2026-07-29_ex991pressrelease07-29x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C04

Weakness: shareholder returns and growth projects compete with deleveraging. Evidence is FY2025 payouts of 92.67% of free cash flow, a USD 750 million repurchase authorization and USD 460 million to USD 500 million of announced Rockingham and First Turn investment. The mechanism is that debt-funded returns or projects would lift leverage again, which leaves recovery to depend on management restraint. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C03

Weakness: floating-rate exposure and a bank facility tied to the notes. Evidence is the revolver-funded redemption of the USD 600 million 2027 notes and a springing maturity linked to the 2028 notes. The mechanism is that fixed coupon debt is replaced by debt that reprices and that bank maturities can be pulled forward, which raises cash interest and refinancing risk if markets are shut. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Casino Salem was the last completed acquisition: on August 27, 2025 the company bought 90% of the equity of Casino Salem for a base price of USD 180 million, recorded as an asset acquisition with a USD 197 million gaming rights intangible, and funded it with revolver borrowings. The company then redevelops the site as Rockingham Grand Casino, with USD 180 million to USD 200 million planned and a mid-2027 opening. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 66; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1

The financing changed materially in September and October 2026. On September 25, 2026 the company closed the eighth amendment to the Credit Agreement, extending the revolver and term loan A to September 2031 with a springing maturity, and entered a new USD 500 million term loan B due 2033 at 99.875% priced at SOFR plus 175 basis points; proceeds repaid the 2028 term loan B and part of the revolver. A conditional redemption notice for the 2027 notes was issued on September 18, 2026 and the notes were redeemed on October 19, 2026 with revolver borrowings, so the debt table at 2026-09-30 still shows them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

Other transactions are the re-acquisition on August 3, 2026 of the 49% of United Tote held by NYRA (with NYRA's tote services agreement extended through 2035), the Preakness Stakes and Black-Eyed Susan Stakes intellectual property purchase for USD 85 million agreed on April 21, 2026 and not reported as closed, and the new USD 750 million repurchase program approved on October 27, 2026, which includes USD 306 million left under the earlier program. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-28_ex991pressrelease10-28x26.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-03-31_chdn-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

fields.value: Capital allocation is the main ownership-related risk. fields.value: Expansion is debt-funded before it earns: Casino Salem is being redeveloped as Rockingham Grand Casino with USD 180 million to USD 200 million of planned investment for a mid-2027 opening, a USD 280 million to USD 300 million building at Churchill Downs Racetrack is planned by the 2028 Kentucky Derby, and a USD 85 million Preakness purchase was agreed in April 2026 with its closing not stated. These commitments compete with debt reduction in 2027 and 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No sponsor, equity support, drop-down, priming or amendment-and-extension behaviour against creditors is documented. The September 2026 bank amendment extended maturities, and the largest related-party style transaction, the repurchase of one million shares from an affiliate of The Duchossois Group in 2023, was approved by the board separately and funded with cash and credit facility borrowings. Legal capacity for restricted payments and debt cannot be tested because no executed financing documents were supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the 2026 record: buybacks fell to USD 44 million in nine months from USD 396 million a year earlier, revolver borrowings fell by USD 578 million, the bank facilities were extended to September 2031, and the dividend has risen for sixteen consecutive years and is small against free cash flow. A diversified base of ten owned casinos, many racing and historical racing venues and a flagship event also limits single-asset risk. The view would turn adverse if buybacks under the new USD 750 million authorization were funded with revolver draws, if the USD 85 million Preakness purchase or the Rockingham investment were financed by borrowing without offsetting repayment, or if the proxy statement or financing documents showed a concentrated holder or loose restricted-payment baskets. It would improve if covenant ratios and indenture terms confirmed tight limits on distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financing changed materially in September and October 2026. On September 25, 2026 the company closed the eighth amendment to the Credit Agreement, extending the revolver and term loan A to September 2031 with a springing maturity, and entered a new USD 500 million term loan B due 2033 at 99.875% priced at SOFR plus 175 basis points; proceeds repaid the 2028 term loan B and part of the revolver. A conditional redemption notice for the 2027 notes was issued on September 18, 2026 and the notes were redeemed on October 19, 2026 with revolver borrowings, so the debt table at 2026-09-30 still shows them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other transactions are the re-acquisition on August 3, 2026 of the 49% of United Tote held by NYRA (with NYRA's tote services agreement extended through 2035), the Preakness Stakes and Black-Eyed Susan Stakes intellectual property purchase for USD 85 million agreed on April 21, 2026 and not reported as closed, and the new USD 750 million repurchase program approved on October 27, 2026, which includes USD 306 million left under the earlier program.

Countervailing evidence is the USD 578 million repayment of revolver borrowings in nine months 2026 and the extension of the bank facilities to September 2031; legal capacity is separate and is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Churchill Downs Inc as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the fundamental credit view: business and operating model, cash flow durability, financial profile, refinancing position, the primary downside path and monitoring triggers. It uses the supplied financial foundation and business and governance analyses and makes no covenant, legal-priority, recovery or relative-value conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Churchill Downs is a cash-generative, seasonal racing and casino operator whose leverage has fallen to 4.08x reported EBITDA, which supports creditors, but the bank facilities' springing maturity makes the notes due in January 2028 the key refinancing test.

fields.value: Business quality is adequate and event-concentrated: Live and Historical Racing earns the largest share of segment profit, and the second quarter produced 37.42% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA, so one flagship event and historical racing machine rules in Kentucky and Virginia carry a large part of the debt service capacity. The 16 historical racing venues, ten owned casinos and online wagering give geographic spread that single-asset operators lack.

fields.value: Cash flow conversion is solid: last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 529.9 million is 45.79% of reported EBITDA, with capital expenditure well below the FY2025 level, but conversion in 2026 benefits from lower project capital and the planned Rockingham and First Turn projects will absorb cash again.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is improving but still material: total debt is 4.08x and net debt 3.94x last-twelve-months reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, down from 4.83x at 2025-12-31, and cash interest cover is 4.22x against 3.61x. On the issuer's Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back its share of equity investees' EBITDA, total leverage is 3.79x.

fields.value: Liquidity is adequate: unrestricted cash of USD 167 million and about USD 1,111 million of undrawn revolver capacity give 1.83x cover of the USD 700 million notes due in January 2028, but the October 2026 redemption of the 2027 notes was funded from the revolver, so the post-redemption position is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing depends on the 2028 notes: the revolver and term loan A, USD 1,148 million at 2026-09-30, mature in September 2031 only if notes maturing earlier are refinanced at least 91 days before maturity, a test that falls on 2027-10-16 for the 2028 notes; the longest-dated debt is the USD 500 million term loan B due 2033. No large note maturity falls before January 2028 after the 2027 redemption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is the main judgement: dividends are small, but FY2025 buybacks and dividends took 92.67% of free cash flow with revolver borrowings rising, while payouts were 15.50% in nine months 2026. Sponsor and governance risk is medium, with no sponsor, no documented creditor-adverse action and legal capacity not testable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a constructive view is that leverage of 4.08x reported EBITDA is still material for a business whose earnings fall in one quarter, that Adjusted EBITDA flatters leverage by including the share of equity investees' EBITDA whose cash reaches the company only as distributions, and that the interest rate exposure rises after the revolver-funded redemption of the 2027 notes. A further weakness is that covenant ratios for 2026 and the definition of the quoted net bank leverage of 3.8x are not printed. The view would weaken if buybacks under the new USD 750 million authorization are funded with revolver draws, if the 2028 notes are not refinanced before the test date, if Virginia historical racing earnings keep falling after the new tax, or if the post-redemption revolver balance shows liquidity well below the USD 1,278 million seen at 2026-09-30. It would strengthen if the next quarterly report shows revolver repayment continuing and covenant ratios with wide headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: the business is spread across racing, wagering and casino earnings. Evidence is that Live and Historical Racing, Wagering Services and Solutions and Gaming produced USD 637.0 million, USD 177.3 million and USD 483.0 million of FY2025 segment Adjusted EBITDA, so no single segment exceeds half of the total. The mechanism is that a shock to one segment is cushioned by the others, which supports debt service capacity and refinancing confidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: cash generation and deleveraging. Evidence is last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 529.9 million and a fall in total debt to reported EBITDA from 4.83x to 4.08x in nine months. The mechanism is that operating cash flow after capital expenditure was applied to the revolver, which shortens the time to a lower leverage level and widens the cushion for the 2028 refinancing.

Evidence is the September 2026 amendment moving the revolver and term loan A to September 2031 and USD 1,278 million of cash and undrawn revolver capacity at 2026-09-30. The mechanism is that no bank maturity falls before 2031 unless the springing test is triggered, so near-term refinancing pressure is limited.

Evidence is 37.42% of FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA in the second quarter and a USD 10 million decrease in Central Virginia Adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026 from competition and a new tax. The mechanism is that a weather, regulatory or tax event concentrates loss in a few states and one quarter, so leverage and liquidity can move sharply.

fields.value: Weakness: shareholder returns and growth projects compete with deleveraging. Evidence is FY2025 payouts of 92.67% of free cash flow, a USD 750 million repurchase authorization and USD 460 million to USD 500 million of announced Rockingham and First Turn investment. The mechanism is that debt-funded returns or projects would lift leverage again, which leaves recovery to depend on management restraint.

fields.value: Weakness: floating-rate exposure and a bank facility tied to the notes. Evidence is the revolver-funded redemption of the USD 600 million 2027 notes and a springing maturity linked to the 2028 notes. The mechanism is that fixed coupon debt is replaced by debt that reprices and that bank maturities can be pulled forward, which raises cash interest and refinancing risk if markets are shut.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Churchill Downs operates the Kentucky Derby venue, 16 historical racing venues in Kentucky and Virginia, online horse wagering and wagering technology, and ten wholly owned and two equity-investee casinos. Revenue is largely transactional and discretionary, tied to attendance, wagering and gaming volume, so cash flow visibility is lower than for contracted businesses, but it is regulated, licensed and spread across many venues, which supports debt service in ordinary conditions and refinancing confidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The company is publicly listed with about 1,940 holders of record and no sponsor or controlling owner identified, so there is no sponsor equity cure and no sponsor-driven recapitalisation in the documents, and creditors depend on board and management financial policy. Casino Salem is 90% owned, two casinos are equity-accounted investees, and the subsidiary guarantors and collateral terms are not printed, so structurally senior claims and restricted group boundaries are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue growth is slowing: net revenue rose 7.01% in FY2025 and 3.50% in nine months 2026, with volume from new venues in Kentucky and Virginia offset by competition and tax in Central Virginia. Pricing power is limited because wagering is a pass-through of pari-mutuel commissions and gaming taxes are set by states, so revenue is cyclical, regulated and exposed to substitution from other gaming and betting, and growth depends on new venues rather than price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have been stable: Adjusted EBITDA margin was 42.39% in FY2024, 41.19% in FY2025 and 42.67% in nine months 2026 against 42.39% a year earlier. Pari-mutuel taxes and purses of USD 349.4 million against Live and Historical Racing segment revenue of USD 1,442.4 million and gaming taxes are variable with volume, which protects margin in a downturn, while salaries, maintenance and venue costs are fixed and create operating leverage when attendance falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA converts to free cash flow at 45.79% on a last-twelve-months basis, helped by distributions from investees and by project capital falling to USD 119 million in nine months 2026 from USD 172 million. Capital expenditure is largely discretionary until committed, but the Rockingham investment of USD 180 million to USD 200 million and the First Turn building of USD 280 million to USD 300 million are committed, and deferred revenue from advance Derby receipts unwinds through the year, so cash conversion is seasonal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_chdn-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_chdn-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; EX-99.1_2026-04-22_ex991pressrelease04-22x26.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competition from other casinos, sports betting and other states' historical racing venues is the main force, buyer power is low because customers are individual patrons, and licensing and tax barriers limit new entrants but are set by states and can change. Macro, regulatory and tax factors are credit drivers only through gaming and pari-mutuel regulation, which the monitoring triggers cover; other macro and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months tailwinds are the full-year effect of new Kentucky and Virginia venues, lower interest cost from debt repayment and extended bank maturities; headwinds are the Virginia tax and competition effect, the revolver-funded note redemption, committed project capital and the January 2028 notes. Over three to five years the opening of Rockingham and the First Turn building add earnings capacity only if funded without lifting leverage, and the sector remains exposed to state policy.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A supported downside begins with a poor Kentucky Derby week or a regulatory or tax change in Kentucky or Virginia, which would first cut second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, the quarter that supplies 37.42% of the year. Lower earnings would raise leverage from 4.08x and reduce free cash flow, and with the revolver already used for the 2027 redemption and a buyback authorization of USD 750 million, management levers are to cut buybacks and project capital, which are discretionary. Liquidity of USD 1,278 million at 2026-09-30 and no bank maturity before 2031 mean resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress unless the 2028 notes are not refinanced by the springing test date, when about USD 1,148 million of bank debt could be pulled forward.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Churchill Downs presents an adequate business profile supported by regional diversification, regulated venues and a flagship event, but credit quality is constrained by event and regulatory concentration, committed project capital and shareholder-return capacity. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow is 45.79% of reported EBITDA, and refinancing capacity is likely to depend on cash flow, revolver availability and the refinancing of the USD 700 million notes due in January 2028. The primary downside path is a weak Kentucky Derby quarter or a Virginia or Kentucky rule change that lifts leverage while buybacks and projects continue. Further analysis would require the post-redemption revolver balance, 2026 covenant ratios and the executed financing documents. Top risk: refinancing the January 2028 notes before the bank facilities' springing maturity test.
